COURT'S OR JUDGE'S ORDERS
Compounding Application No. 1 of 2024
In
C 482 No. 715 of 2024
Hon'ble Rakesh Thapliyal, J.
1. Mr. R.K. Rawat, learned counsel holding brief of
Mr. Sanjeev Singh, learned counsel for the applicant.
2. Mr. B.C. Joshi, learned Assistant Government
Advocate for the State.
3. Mr. Niranjan Bhatt, learned counsel for the
respondent nos. 2 and 3.
4. Present C-482 application has been preferred
along with compounding application supported with
the affidavits of applicant and respondent nos. 2 and 3.
5. Applicant along with his brother - Nasruddeen
and respondent no. 3 - victim, daughter of respondent
no. 2 - complainant along with her mother - Faimeeda
and respondent no. 2, all are present in person before
this Court and they are identified by their respective
counsel.
6. Brief facts of the present case are that
respondent no. 2 lodged the First Information Report
dated 27.10.2021, Police Station - Basant Vihar, District
Dehradun bearing FIR No. 211 of 2021 for the offences
punishable under Section 363 IPC with regard to
missing of her daughter, who at that time was
studying in Class X. Present applicant was named in
the FIR and after investigation, charge-sheet was filed
and the applicant was summoned for the offences
punishable under Section 363, 376 IPC and under
Section 5/6 of the POCSO Act, 2012 and the trial is
pending in the court of Special Judge, POCSO / FTC /
Addl. Sessions Judge, Dehradun. Applicant applied
for bail before this Court and the Coordinate Bench of
this Court by order dated 24.11.2022 enlarged the
applicant on bail. While enlarging the applicant on
bail, the Coordinate Bench of this Court has also
examined the submissions of learned counsel for the
applicant that the victim is wife of the applicant and
both are married and they were in relationship and the
victim in her statement recorded under Section 164
Cr.P.C., admitted this fact.
7. Now, the compounding application has been
moved with this contention that the applicant is
married with respondent no. 3 - victim, who is
daughter of respondent no. 2, on 21.11.2023 and in

2024:UHC:6441
support of which marriage certificate is also enclosed.
It is also submitted that on the date, when the
marriage was solemnized, victim was major, since her
date of birth was 19.10.2005, as per Adhar Card and
there is no dispute about her age. It is also submitted
that respondent no. 3 - victim is now 7 months'
pregnant from the present applicant and if the
proceeding is permitted to be continued, it will spoil
the married life of respondent no. 3.
8. Per contra, learned State Counsel submits that
after thorough investigation, charge-sheet was filed
and offences are not compoundable and on the date of
commission of crime, victim was minor. However, he
has not denied this fact that the victim in her statement
recorded under Section 164 Cr.P.C. admitted that she
was in relationship with the applicant and now,
married with the applicant, the reference of which has
been given in the order dated 24.11.2022 passed by the
Coordinate Bench of this Court in B.A. 1st No. 2598 of
2022. Apart from this, he submits that offences are
serious in nature. However, he fairly submits that
since now, applicant married with respondent no. 3 -
victim and she is also 7 months' pregnant from the
applicant, therefore, in order to save their married life,
proceedings may be quashed. He further submits that
since the victim in her statement recorded under
Section 164 Cr.P.C. admitted that she was in
relationship with the applicant and married with the
applicant, therefore, there is no useful purpose to
continue with the proceeding, since there are now
remote chances of conviction.
9. After taking into consideration fact that the
applicant is married with the respondent no. 3 - victim
and she is 7 months' pregnant from the applicant,
therefore, in order to save their marriage, this Court is
of the view that compounding application deserves to
be allowed. Accordingly, compounding application is
allowed.
10. Entire proceedings of Special Session Trial No.
33 of 2022 (State Vs. Samshuddin @ Chotu) offences
punishable under Section 363, 376 IPC and under
Section 5/6 of the POCSO Act, 2012 pending in the
court of Special Judge, POCSO / FTC / Addl. Sessions
Judge, Dehradun are quashed.
11. C482 application is disposed of accordingly
 (Rakesh Thapliyal, J.)
 05.09.2024
SKS
